payload.claim: `citations_held_at(mirror, commit, text)` (called by `_stack_cite` at the spec's own historical commit, saffron/cli.py:1314) recomputes `suffixes` from that commit's own tree, while `citation_defects` for the same text (saffron/cli.py:1318, saffron/spec_citations.py:353-354) recomputes `suffixes` independently from the later `head` commit's tree. `_is_path_shaped` (line 81) uses that suffix set to decide whether a backtick token is even recognized as a citation, so if a file suffix present at `head` did not yet exist in the tree at the spec's own commit (or vice versa), the same text can be tokenized into a different citation list at the two commits, and the held map's offsets then fail to line up with the defects' offsets for the citation whose shape classification changed. No test constructs a spec whose own commit and whose review-head commit have different file-suffix sets, so this holds in every fixture (`cite_repo`'s suffix set never changes between commits) but is not guaranteed on a real repo, where new file types are added between a spec's own commit and the batch's head.
